verdict_rule: PCMB: no reference implementation exists, so each row sets Andrey's mean beside the paper's mean and standard deviation (Table 6), and the release card judges no row better or worse. The floor: per dataset, the mean over the targets of the errors minus the empty set's; a row passes when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of the mean difference lies wholly below 0 over at least 10 datasets, and the per-dataset differences are in the row | GS, Fast-IAMB, and HITON-PC: per cell (network or Gaussian graph, rows; 20 datasets, every node a target): per dataset, the mean over the targets with a nonempty true set of the distance of the set's precision and recall from (1, 1) (an empty answer counts precision 1, distance 1) and of the set's F1; D = Andrey's minus bnlearn's per dataset; worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of the mean D lies wholly on the worse side of 0 (10,000 resamples of the datasets, default_rng(0)), better when wholly on the better side, a tie otherwise. A cell worse on seeds 0-19 on either measure was rerun on seeds 20-39 and is worse only when the fresh seeds agree; a cell better on seeds 0-19 was not rerun | CMB: no reference implementation exists, so each row sets Andrey's means beside the paper's (Table 1) and judges CMB against two global PCs read at the target, Andrey's pc with the same test and level and bnlearn 5.2.1 pc.stable with mi-adf: the mean over paired datasets of CMB's total minus the other's with its 95% percentile-bootstrap interval, better or worse when the interval lies wholly on that side of 0 over at least 10 datasets, on seeds 0-19, and a cell worse there counts only when it is worse again on seeds 20-39. The floor: per dataset, the total minus the empty answer's; a row passes when its interval lies wholly below 0 | HITON-MB: per cell (network, rows; 20 datasets): per dataset, the mean over the targets both answered with a nonempty true set of the distance of the set's precision and recall from (1, 1) (an empty answer counts precision 1, distance 1) and of the set's F1; D = Andrey's minus Causal Explorer's per dataset; worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of the mean D lies wholly on the worse side of 0 (10,000 resamples of the datasets, default_rng(0)), better when wholly on the better side, a tie otherwise. A cell worse on seeds 0-19 on either measure was rerun on seeds 20-39 and is worse only when the fresh seeds agree; a cell better on seeds 0-19 was not rerun. A target where the toolbox stopped without an answer is left out of both sides | MMB-by-MMB: per cell (network, rows; 20 datasets, the paper's named targets): per dataset, the mean over the targets with a true edge of the distance of the precision and recall of the edges at the target from (1, 1) and of their F1, an edge right only with both marks right (an answer with no edge counts precision 1, distance 1, F1 0); D = Andrey's minus the authors' code's per dataset; worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of the mean D lies wholly on the worse side of 0 (10,000 resamples of the datasets, default_rng(0)), better when wholly on the better side, a tie otherwise. A cell worse on seeds 0-19 on either measure was rerun on seeds 20-39 and is worse only when the fresh seeds agree | Y-structures: per cell (setting, with or without selection, form; 20 datasets of 10,000 rows from the authors' simulation script): per dataset, claim_error and claim_ap_loss; D = Andrey's minus the authors' code's per dataset; worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of the mean D lies wholly above 0 (10,000 resamples of the datasets, default_rng(0)), better when wholly below, a tie otherwise. A cell worse on seeds 0-19 on either measure is rerun on seeds 20-39 and is worse only when the fresh seeds agree; a cell better on seeds 0-19 is not rerun. The floor: claim_error minus the empty answer's, applied where the authors' code's interval lies wholly below 0, passed when Andrey's interval lies wholly below 0; every row also gives the precision floor, passed when the pooled precision exceeds the pooled base rate with its 95% interval above 0 | LDECC and LOAD: per cell (20 datasets, seeds 0-19, one treatment-outcome pair each): per dataset D = Andrey's error minus the authors' code's on the same data; worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of the mean D lies wholly above 0 (10,000 resamples of the datasets, default_rng(0)), better when wholly below, a tie otherwise. A cell worse on seeds 0-19 on a measure was rerun on seeds 20-39 and is worse only when the fresh seeds agree. The floor: per dataset, the error minus the empty adjustment set's (for LOAD's set, the set's missing plus extra members against the empty set's, an answer with no set counting as the empty set); it applies where the authors' code's interval lies wholly below 0, and a row then passes when Andrey's does too | MB-by-MB: no reference implementation exists, so each row sets Andrey's means beside the paper's (Tables 1-3) and judges MB-by-MB against two global PCs read at the target, Andrey's pc and bnlearn 5.2.1 pc.stable with mi-adf, both with the same test and level and at most 5 conditioning variables, the paper's cap, and against Andrey's CMB at the same level where it ran: the mean over paired datasets of MB-by-MB's shd minus the other's with its 95% percentile-bootstrap interval, better or worse when the interval lies wholly on that side of 0 over at least 10 datasets, on the first seeds, and a cell worse there counts only when it is worse again on the fresh seeds. A comparison dominates a cell when it is more accurate and takes fewer tests per answer; the tests over every target are context. The floor: per dataset, the shd minus the empty answer's; a row passes when its interval lies wholly below 0 | LocPC-CDE: per cell (20 datasets, seeds 0-19, one treatment-outcome pair each): per dataset D = Andrey's error minus the authors' code's on the same data; worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of the mean D lies wholly above 0 (10,000 resamples of the datasets, default_rng(0)), better when wholly below, a tie otherwise. A cell worse on seeds 0-19 on a measure was rerun on seeds 20-39 and is worse only when the fresh seeds agree. The floor, per dataset: the verdict error minus the constant 'not identifiable' answer's (1 on identifiable pairs, 0 on the others), the set's missing plus extra members minus the empty set's, and the effect error minus the unadjusted regression's; it applies where the authors' code's interval lies wholly below 0, and a row then passes when Andrey's does too | Local ISA-LiNG: per cell (graph, rows, blanket; 20 datasets, one target each): D = Andrey's minus the authors' code's SHD of the local graph and Euclidean weight distance per dataset, on the datasets both finished; worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of the mean D lies wholly above 0 (10,000 resamples of the datasets, default_rng(0)), better when wholly below, a tie otherwise. A cell worse on seeds 0-19 was rerun on seeds 20-39 and is worse only when the fresh seeds agree | MMMB: per cell (network, rows; 20 datasets): per dataset, the mean over the targets both answered with a nonempty true set of the distance of the set's precision and recall from (1, 1) (an empty answer counts precision 1, distance 1) and of the set's F1; D = Andrey's minus Causal Explorer's per dataset; worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of the mean D lies wholly on the worse side of 0 (10,000 resamples of the datasets, default_rng(0)), better when wholly on the better side, a tie otherwise. A cell worse on seeds 0-19 on either measure was rerun on seeds 20-39 and is worse only when the fresh seeds agree; a cell better on seeds 0-19 was not rerun. A target where the toolbox stopped without an answer is left out of both sides | DAGMA: per cell (noise, scale, graph, variables; 20 datasets): D = SHD(Andrey) - SHD(reference) per dataset, on the datasets both fitted; worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of mean D lies entirely above 0, better when entirely below, a tie otherwise (10,000 resamples of the datasets, default_rng(0)). The decision cells are the z-scored ones (claim in), 24: ER2 and SF4, 10 to 100 variables, three noises; the raw cells, where the least-squares fit reads the simulation's units, and the rescaled cells are reported, not judged (claim out), at 10 to 50 variables. No decision cell was worse than the reference, so none was rerun; the one rescaled cell worse on seeds 0-19 (SF4, 50 variables, Gaussian noise) was rerun on seeds 20-39 and is a tie there. The floor, per dataset: SHD(Andrey) minus SHD(empty graph); it applies where the reference's interval lies wholly below 0, and a row then passes when Andrey's does too. On the z-scored cells it applies in none: the reference is below the empty graph in none of the 24 | LDP and LD3: per cell (20 datasets, seeds 0-19, one treatment-outcome pair each): per dataset D = Andrey's error minus the authors' code's on the same data; worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of the mean D lies wholly above 0 (10,000 resamples of the datasets, default_rng(0)), better when wholly below, a tie otherwise (a tie too when the two errors are equal on every dataset). A cell worse on seeds 0-19 on a measure is rerun on seeds 20-39 and is worse only when the fresh seeds agree. The floor: per dataset, the error minus the floor's (the empty adjustment set for valid_set_loss, parents_error, and effect_error; for LD3's direct_error the better constant answer over the 40 datasets of a size with and without the direct effect); it applies where the authors' code's interval lies wholly below 0, and a row then passes when Andrey's does too

The same level on both arms: Fisher's z at 0.01 on the Gaussian cells (the papers' level) and Pearson's chi-square at 0.001 on MILDEW (LDP's Figure 6), where Andrey refers the statistic to its mean under a shuffle (its default degrees of freedom) and the authors' code to (r - 1)(c - 1) per configuration over the values present
error_metric: PCMB: distance: the mean over a dataset's targets with a nonempty answer of the distance of the set's precision and recall from (1, 1), the reading of the comparison with the paper: an empty answer has no precision or distance and counts in the recall as 0; distance_one counts an empty answer as distance 1; precision is the mean over the targets with an answer and recall the mean over all targets. The floor uses the set's errors, missing plus extra members, against the empty set's, the true set's size; every value is a mean over the row's datasets, and andrey_s is the median wall time of a fit for every target | GS, Fast-IAMB, and HITON-PC: set_distance: the mean over the targets of the distance of the set's precision and recall from (1, 1); set_f1_loss: 1 minus the mean over the targets of the set's F1. The floor uses the set's errors, missing plus extra members (the wrong answers of andrey.metrics.target_answer_scores), against the empty set's, the true set's size | CMB: total: per target, the edges at the target missing or extra against the true CPDAG plus those whose direction differs from it, an edge the CPDAG directs and the answer leaves undirected included (reversed); a dataset's value is the mean over its targets. lenient leaves out the undirected ones. The floor uses the total against the empty answer's, the target's degree | HITON-MB: set_distance: the mean over the targets of the distance of the set's precision and recall from (1, 1); set_f1_loss: 1 minus the mean over the targets of the set's F1. The floor uses the set's errors, missing plus extra members (the wrong answers of andrey.metrics.target_answer_scores), against the empty set's, the true set's size | MMB-by-MMB: edge_distance: the mean over the targets of the distance of the precision and recall of the edges at the target from (1, 1), an edge right only with both endpoint marks right; edge_f1_loss: 1 minus the mean over the targets of their F1. The floor uses the local endpoint SHD at the target (extra, missing, and mismarked edges) against the empty answer's, the target's true degree | Y-structures: claim_error: per dataset, the claimed ancestral pairs that are false plus the true ancestral pairs not claimed, among the system variables; claim_ap_loss: 1 minus the average precision of the ranking by the claims' scores, the pairs not claimed last. The floor uses claim_error against the empty answer's, the number of true pairs, so their difference is the false claims minus the true ones. precision_floor is the precision of the pooled claims minus the pooled base rate, the precision of claiming every pair | LDECC and LOAD: LDECC: family_error, 1 when the parent sets returned are not the family of the treatment's parent sets the true CPDAG allows; recall_loss, 1 when the treatment's true parents are not among them; hausdorff_mse, the squared Hausdorff distance of the effects estimated with the sets from the population effects of the family, in standard deviations; effect_error, the mean absolute error of the estimated effects on a fresh sample. LOAD: set_f1_loss, 1 minus the F1 of the returned set against the optimal adjustment set for the pair asked (no set counts F1 0); effect_error as for LDECC | MB-by-MB: shd: per target, the edges at the target against the true DAG, an edge the answer leaves undirected (undirected), a true edge it misses (miss), an edge the DAG lacks (extra), and a directed edge whose direction differs (reverse), shd their sum; a dataset's value is the mean over its targets. The floor uses the shd against the empty answer's, the target's degree. Cost per answer, what answering one target costs: MB-by-MB's and CMB's tests at that target, a global PC's whole fit; cost over every target: their sum over the targets, the one fit | LocPC-CDE: verdict_error: 1 when the answer's identifiable is not the truth's (the true CPDAG directs every edge at the outcome, or not), an undecided or missing answer included, so that 1 minus its mean is the paper's identifiable proportion; parents_error (identifiable pairs): 1 unless the answer is identifiable with the outcome's true parents other than the treatment as its set; effect_error (linear-Gaussian identifiable pairs): the absolute error, in standard deviations, of the direct effect estimated by least squares of the outcome on the treatment and the set on a fresh sample, paired over the datasets where both arms gave a set | Local ISA-LiNG: shd: the paper's SHD of the local graph, the edges into and out of the target and into each of its children in each graph, counted as the authors' code counts it (adjacencies one side has and the other lacks, plus edges whose reverse is true); weight_distance: the Euclidean norm of the difference of the two local weight matrices. The floor is each against the empty answer's (the true local edges' count and norm) | MMMB: set_distance: the mean over the targets of the distance of the set's precision and recall from (1, 1); set_f1_loss: 1 minus the mean over the targets of the set's F1. The floor uses the set's errors, missing plus extra members (the wrong answers of andrey.metrics.target_answer_scores), against the empty set's, the true set's size | DAGMA: SHD of the DAG against the true DAG (a reversed edge counts 1), the papers' measure: andrey_shd, comparator_shd, and empty_shd are medians over the paired datasets, and the _mean fields their means. The _mec_ fields and mec are the SHD between the CPDAGs of the estimate and of the truth, reported and not judged | LDP and LD3: valid_set_loss: 1 when LDP returns no adjustment set or a set that is not a valid adjustment set for the pair in the true DAG (hidden variables included), else 0; effect_error: the mean absolute error of the effect estimated with the returned set on a fresh sample, in standard deviations (a set-free answer has none); parents_error: 1 unless LD3's set is the outcome's true parents other than the treatment; direct_error: 1 when the answer's nonzero for the direct effect is not the truth's (an edge from the treatment to the outcome)

regimes.discrete: net:<network>:<rows>: forward samples of the bnlearn repository network, columns that hold one value left out of every fit, each answering the empty set at its target, every set scored against the whole network
regimes.gaussian: gauss:<d>:<rows>[:<mean degree>]: linear-Gaussian Erdos-Renyi graph, standardized, mean degree 2 unless given
regimes.latent_networks: the paper's four networks (MILDEW, ALARM, WIN95PTS, ANDES) as linear-Gaussian models, weights +-U(0.5, 1), N(0, 1) noise, 4/4/6/10 random non-target nodes hidden, columns shuffled; the truth is the PAG of the observed variables, read at each target
regimes.selection: setting:<fixed|small|large>: linear-Gaussian models of the authors' simulation script, 10,000 rows kept when the sum of the selection variables lies in [2, 2.5], the system columns in an order drawn from the seed and the context last

regimes.identifiable_cde_gaussian: locpc-identifiable@5000,v=<d>: the paper's linear-Gaussian DAGs with a pair whose controlled direct effect the true CPDAG identifies
regimes.identifiable_cde_binary: locpc-identifiable@5000,family=binary,v=<d>: the same with the paper's logistic binary model
regimes.nonidentifiable_cde_gaussian: locpc-nonidentifiable@5000,v=<d>: the paper's linear-Gaussian DAGs with a pair whose controlled direct effect the true CPDAG does not identify
regimes.nonidentifiable_cde_binary: locpc-nonidentifiable@5000,family=binary,v=<d>: the same with the paper's logistic binary model
